mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 4% in the month prior to the decision is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to reduced risk appetite and compressed credit spreads.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.0% in the preceding month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during such FEDFUNDS spikes (p > 0.05), or credit spreads widen instead of narrowing.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate falls by more than 0.2 percentage points in the month before the decision, labor market strength is interpreted as supportive of equity valuations, driving positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE decreases by >0.2pp in the prior month
regime_hint: Early in an economic recovery phase
failure_condition: No significant positive return in 20 days after such UNRATE declines, or alternative indicators (e.g., payroll growth) show weakness.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in industrial production exceeding 2% signals weakening supply-side demand, which predicts negative 60-day S&P 500 forward returns as investors anticipate softening business activity.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines >2% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during such INDPRO declines (p > 0.10), or alternative demand proxies (e.g., retail sales) show strength.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) of over 0.5% in the month prior to the decision is interpreted as a supply shock, producing a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as inflation expectations fall.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL drops >0.5% in the prior month
failure_condition: No significant positive 20-day return during such CPIAUCSL declines, or core inflation (ex-CPIAUCSL) rises instead.

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS falls below 2%, the anticipation of future rate cuts is expected to boost equity valuations, yielding a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are flat or negative despite the FEDFUNDS signal, or rate cuts do not materialize.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) by over 50,000 in a single month predicts stronger labor demand, which is associated with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >50,000 in a single month
failure_condition: No positive 20-day return after such payroll gains, or other labor indicators (e.g., hours worked) show weakness.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly declines in the S&P 500's own monthly index (HOUST) of 3% or more indicate extreme bearish sentiment, leading to negative 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls >3% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during such declines, or alternative sentiment indicators (e.g., VIX) show calm.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in consumer confidence (not directly observable here, but as a proxy via RSAFS falling >10%) suggests weakening demand, resulting in a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS decreases by >10% in the prior month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during such RSAFS drops, or alternative sentiment proxies (if available) contradict the signal.
